column3: Says Dinah went out “to see” the daughters of the land, rather than specifying a visit.
Expresses violating her with a separate verb after “lay with her,” rather than the adverbial phrase “by force.”
His soul “clung” to Dinah, and he “spoke to the girl’s heart,” retaining the bodily image rendered “spoke to her tenderly.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Retains an unnamed “he” as the defiler and repeats Jacob as the one keeping silent, rather than supplying Shechem’s name.
Close to the Hebrew.
The men’s anger is expressed as burning intensely, rather than simply being filled with fury.
Retains his soul as the subject of longing, rather than only saying “My son Shechem longs.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Let me find favor in your eyes” retains the image and the request for favor rather than “Grant me this favor.”
Names a bride-price and a gift, with a shared command to increase them greatly, rather than separate adjectives “high” and “expensive.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Describes the man as having a foreskin rather than only calling him “uncircumcised.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Says “our daughter,” rather than changing the relationship to “our sister.”
Their words are good “in the eyes of” Hamor and “in the eyes of” Shechem, repeating the image rather than saying their offer seemed good.
Close to the Hebrew.

Retains the hand image in describing the spacious land and its position “before them.”

Repeats “all those going out of the gate of his city” after the circumcision statement.
Dates the attack “on the third day,” rather than “Three days later.”
“By the mouth of the sword” retains the singular sword and its mouth image rather than “with their swords.”
Does not add “other” before Jacob’s sons. The final clause is active plural, “they had defiled their sister,” rather than passive.
Close to the Hebrew.
The final house is singular rather than the plural “their houses.”
The statement about few numbers begins with singular “I,” rather than “We.” The gathering and attack follow as statements joined by “and,” rather than an explicit “if” clause.
